h: Gardens, Gates and a Bit of Wildlife
p: Warrington makes it easy to mix active fun with a quieter few hours. Walton Hall and Gardens, on the south side of town, has grand Victorian gardens, woodland walks and plenty of space for a picnic. It's a great choice if the kids still have energy after the trampolines, or if you want somewhere more relaxed to finish the day.

Families with younger children often head to Gulliver's World, a theme park aimed squarely at little ones with rides and themed areas, so it's worth knowing about if you're planning a weekend with kids of different ages. Older kids might enjoy a walk through Sankey Valley Park, a long green corridor along the old canal with flat, easy paths.

In the town centre, look out for the Golden Gates outside Warrington Town Hall. These ornate gilded iron gates are a striking sight and a local landmark. Warrington Museum and Art Gallery is also in the centre and free to visit, with displays covering everything from natural history to local life.

For your Gravity session, keep it simple: fill in waivers before you arrive, bring a bottle of water and leave valuables in a locker or at home. Grip socks can usually be reused, so pop them in your bag for next time. Weekends and school holidays are the busiest times, so if you can manage a weekday or term-time slot, you'll often find a bit more room to bounce.
